supporting_observations.claim: The domain controller recorded two failed network logons for kim.nguyen from 192.0.2.88 at 13:45 and 13:46 UTC; both show a bad-password substatus.
At 13:48 UTC, the domain controller recorded a successful network logon for kim.nguyen from the same address, 192.0.2.88, using Kerberos.
The failures followed by a success from the same address warrant investigation, but the records do not establish whether this was legitimate password correction or unauthorized access.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy logs were not collected from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC because of a collection outage, covering the authentication events at 13:45–13:48 UTC.
The authentication records identify the source as 192.0.2.88 but do not identify a corresponding endpoint or person operating it.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish whether 192.0.2.88 belongs to a legitimate device or an unauthorized source.
The evidence does not establish that kim.nguyen or an attacker caused the successful logon.
The evidence does not establish credential compromise, malicious intent, or the reason for the two bad-password attempts.
additional_evidence_needed: Map 192.0.2.88 to a device and owner using available DHCP, IPAM, network, or endpoint records for the relevant time.
Review related domain-controller and authentication records for the source address and account, including subsequent activity associated with the successful logon.
Confirm with kim.nguyen whether the attempts and successful logon were expected.
unrelated_findings: At 14:18 UTC, WS-KNGUYEN-01 accessed drive.google.com and related Google Drive resources. Google Drive is not listed as approved; treat this as a separate finding. The records show access, not file upload or data exfiltration. (T121-00021, T121-00022, T121-00024, T121-00027, T121-00033)
